summary: The Gemara expounds each phrase of Numbers 19 regarding the red heifer, establishes that the Tsuk cliff is 12 mil from Jerusalem, details how the goat is pushed backward, and describes the signal relay system and the crimson thread that turned white as a sign of atonement.

display.whats: What does each phrase in the parah adumah verse teach, and what are the physical details of the Azazel goat ceremony?
display.hint: The Gemara is doing two things simultaneously: a verse-by-verse drasha of Numbers 19 (each word teaches a halakha about the parah rite) and filling in practical details of the Yom Kippur goat journey - the cliff distance, the manner of pushing, the signal system.
display.title: The Parah Verses, the Tsuk, and the Whitening Thread

learning.ahaMoment: The crimson thread turning white is Is. 1:18 fulfilled physically - 'though your sins be red as scarlet, they shall become white as snow.' The Temple era was when this verse was literally enacted.
learning.memoryAnchor: Crimson thread + backward push + 12-mil cliff: the ceremony was designed so there would be no ambiguity that the goat had truly been sent away and could not return.
learning.learnerQuestion: What halakhot does each phrase of the parah adumah verse yield, and what does it mean when the crimson thread fails to turn white?
learning.coreTension: The crimson thread's whitening is treated as a sign that atonement was accepted, but the thread did not always turn white even in Temple times, raising the question of whether the sending itself, not the sign, is what actually achieves atonement.
learning.coreMove: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's warning, 'do not rely on the thread - it is a sign but not the atonement itself,' resolves the tension: the verse-by-verse halakhot (12-mil Tsuk, backward push, signal relay, divided thread) establish a precisely defined ceremony whose efficacy does not depend on the thread turning white.

takeaway.text: The crimson thread turning white is a sign of atonement, not its cause; the goat's sending itself, carried out exactly as the verse-by-verse halakhot specify, is what achieves atonement, whether or not the thread whitens.

learning.learningBlocker: Learners may treat the whitening thread as the mechanism of atonement itself, missing Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's point that it is only a sign and the goat's sending is what actually atones.

rashiTranslations.en: Rashi: opens - a donkey was taken along with the goat - according to the first Tanna [this was permitted], since there is no [scriptural] basis [for prohibiting it].
Rashi: continues - to Shmuel - [the proof is that] it is written 'and [Elazar] the priest shall take' - [this refers to] the taking of [its] blood.
Rashi: continues - [implying] the non-Jew is fit for slaughter - [therefore] it was necessary to write [separately regarding the] taking [of blood, to teach that Elazar alone must perform it].

Rashi: continues - the taking of blood [must be] by Elazar - to return [the word back] to Elazar [from the previous context] - [for] if [the verse] had written '[and he shall take]' [referring to] the blood, it would seem [that] the slaughter [is also done by someone else].
Rashi: continues - and the sprinkling [is written:] 'and he shall sprinkle with his finger' - [this too] would [seem to be done by someone other than Elazar].
Rashi: continues - to Rav - [who] also said [that] the slaughter is [by] Elazar - [therefore] it was not necessary to write [the taking of blood, as the entire ceremony requires Elazar].
Rashi: continues - regarding Elazar, [the scripture] was not [required] to write [about taking blood separately, since] the slaughter is [already taught to be by Elazar].
Rashi: continues - regarding the taking of blood, [the scripture] did write - and if [the word] 'he' is written, [this teaches] a diminution [from the usual rule].
Rashi: continues - after [another] diminution [we have] for Elazar - and [there is] no diminution after diminution [permitted in Torah law].
Rashi: continues - '[therefore:] and the priest shall take cedar' - [this is the next phrase in Numbers 19].
Rashi: continues - [regarding] cedar wood - to Shmuel - [he] said [that] the taking of blood and the sprinkling are [both performed] by Elazar, [as is] written [in the verse].
Rashi: continues - regarding the priest in [general] - it is written [that] the burning and the casting [are also performed by the priest].
Rashi: continues - the casting of cedar wood [is performed] by a common priest - [this is] permitted, [whereas the taking of blood requires Elazar].
Rashi: continues - this [teaching] implies [that] a non-Jew is excluded [from] this [task] - [the text teaches] that [a non-Jew] cannot [perform] the casting.
Rashi: continues - and all of these [tasks] that we have stated - [regarding] the slaughter [and] sprinkling - [are] to Rav - [who rules that they require Elazar].
Rashi: continues - [whether performed] by a common priest - [the text teaches] that it is excluded [from the general rule].
Rashi: continues - and [this exclusion is] not [derived] from [the general scope of] the verse before it - [therefore] it was necessary to write [it separately].
Rashi: continues - that [the priest must perform this act] - [for] if [the verse] had written '[and] he [shall take] cedar wood,' and [it did] not [write] 'priest,' [we would understand].
Rashi: continues - '[that any] one who wishes [may] take [it],' and [there would be] no [basis to] establish him [as needing to be] a priest.
Rashi: continues - [rather, the verse] establishes [him as] a priest, [since it] says [that the priest performs this] - [this is the resolution of the textual difficulty].
Rashi: continues - regarding [the question of whether] a non-Jew [performs the] burning or [whether] Elazar [performs it] - [the Gemara raises the issue].
Rashi: continues - perhaps [we should] say [that since this is not the body [of the ritual], we can infer that] a non-Jew [could perform the] burning.
Rashi: continues - [but the Tanna] teaches [regarding] 'the priest in his office' - this [phrase] 'priest' [appears to be] extra, [it] was not [necessary to write it, except].
Rashi: continues - [to teach something regarding the previous context] - and thus [the word] 'priest' is not [superfluous, but rather].
Rashi: continues - [establishes that the taking of blood and the sprinkling] are [performed by] the priest - and I know [that this is the case from the following].
Rashi: continues - that this [reference] is [made to establish the rule for] the one [who performs] the burning - [the text] stands [as an independent teaching].
Rashi: continues - [regarding] the priest and his garments, [the text] teaches [that he must wash his garments] - [implying that] in the [priest's] garments [of priesthood, the rule] is [applied].
Rashi: continues - [and] not in [the priest's] garments [of ordinary] profane [use] - [this is a crucial limitation of when the rule applies].
Rashi: continues - and [the priest] becomes impure until [the] evening - [this teaches the extent of the impurity].
Rashi: continues - [on] the red heifer [that is] made [for] generations - [implying that for all future] generations, [this halakha applies].
Rashi: continues - [whether performed] by a common priest, and [not] based on the completion of the statute [from] the day [of its original performance].
Rashi: continues - [for the Gemara is asking:] did [the procedure] become [fixed] on the day [Yom Kippur]? [This was] necessary to write [the word] 'priest' here.
Rashi: continues - to teach [that] it [the statute] is [performed] by [priests of all] generations, [not just the] High Priest.
Rashi: continues - [all of whom must wear] the [garments] of priesthood [when performing this] service.
Rashi: continues - '[the verse says:] a man for him to make fit the [stranger]' - from the [preceding verse, it appears that] a priest [is performing this task].
Rashi: continues - [the text] here [says] 'a man' [instead of 'the priest'] - [implying] that a non-priest [could perform this task].
Rashi: continues - [therefore] if [the verse] had written '[and he shall] gather [the ashes] of the heifer,' [we would say].
Rashi: continues - a priest [must gather them, since the previous verses mentioned] 'the priest' [throughout].
Rashi: continues - [now the text] here [writes] 'a man' - [this] 'man' [teaching teaches that] the priest [mentioned] in the previous [context is the basis].
Rashi: continues - 'a man' [to make fit] the woman - [the Gemara continues:] [from what source] do [we derive that] a pure [person].
Rashi: continues - is [required for making fit the woman]? [The fact] that it is written [in the verse - this teaches].
Rashi: continues - [the Gemara brings proof from another verse] the Lord said [concerning the offering].
Rashi: continues - [regarding] the giving of water [to be placed] on the ashes in [a vessel of] earthen [ware].
Rashi: continues - [after the verse states] 'and [he shall] gather' - [which emphasizes] after the gathering [comes the next phase].
Rashi: continues - and it is written '[and they took it]' - [referring to] those [mentioned] in the gathering - [specifically] a non-Jew.
Rashi: continues - and a woman - [but] not a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor.
Rashi: continues - [therefore, if] this [rule applies] - [then] because it stands [in the verse from the previous context, we could] say '[and] he shall take [it].'
Rashi: continues - [implying that] what [is mentioned] regarding the gathering - [in the] singular [form], [the text] has written it.
Rashi: concludes - [regarding] a woman - from where [do we derive this]? - [and] so [too] an androgyne [applies] - because of [its] uncertain [status as a] woman.
Rashi: continues - and the Rabbis - [said] to him: 'For ever you [are] standing in the previous [context] - and from the fact that it is not written '[and] he shall take' [with the] singular [form].
Rashi: continues - [from] this [negative phrasing] - [if the verse] had written '[and] he shall take [it] and [he himself] shall give [it] on the water,' [we would say].
Rashi: continues - 'until [only] one [person] takes [some of] the ashes, and he himself gives it on the water' - it is written '[and] he shall take' [using the singular].
Rashi: continues - [implying that even] if two [people] take [it] - [the rite is still valid].
Rashi: continues - [the verse] and [he shall take] hyssop - [the Gemara continues the discussion of which items are required].
Rashi: continues - [it is written] 'in the sprinkling with the water [of the heifer]' - and this [sprinkling] is [a] work [that occurs] after the sanctification.
Rashi: continues - to the Rabbis - [who] said [that] the sanctification is made [using the ashes] of that [batch] - and in the gathering it is written 'a man.'
Rashi: continues - [meaning] a pure [person] - [this is what] the [verse] means - a non-Jew and a woman [can perform] the gathering - on your life [you must understand it this way].
Rashi: continues - [because] a pure [person here does not mean] to make fit a non-Jew and a woman - [but rather, as it] were [to teach].
Rashi: continues - [the] verse [must] be silent [about this matter], and [instead] it should write '[and] he shall take hyssop and [dip] in water and sprinkle' - and I know [that].
Rashi: continues - [the] fact [is that] in that [gathering, the rule] stands [and comes] from [the previous context] - [so] even if [we wrote] 'a man' [in the sprinkling verse], [we would say].
Rashi: continues - '[this means] not [that] a woman [is excluded]' - on your life [this would be] the implication [from the] directly [stated meaning].
Rashi: continues - [regarding] a pure [person] to make fit a minor - [the Gemara rules:] from [the fact that] he is disqualified [in] the sanctification.
Rashi: continues - [regarding the view] to Rabbi Yehuda - [who] said [that] a woman [is disqualified] in the sanctification, and a minor [is] fit - [therefore the teaching] comes [in reverse order].

Rashi: continues - [teaching that] a man [is required] - not a minor - [and] a pure [person] to make fit [a] woman - [this] of necessity [means that] there is no [way] to say [that] 'a man' [and] 'pure' [means] 'from the implication' [alone].
Rashi: concludes - [this] is the end [of the detailed discussion on the parah adumah specifications and requirements on 43a].
